claims.statement: At the first shell n=2p+2, the complete fixed-selector sum is nonpositive for eligible trees in which every selected leaf-deletion forest has no isolates and has a marked root of degree at least two (the empty selector is vacuous); eligibility also forces tau(H_v)=p+1-(alpha(T)-p) <= floor(p/2)+1. The remaining ordered-root contributions are confined to explicitly described order-2k boundary parts, whose excess is not compensated here.
claims.scope: Ordinary finite trees T with n=2p+2, x(T)+2<=p, 3p<2alpha(T)+1; F(T,p) is the original strict favorable-leaf selector and repeated same-support leaves remain distinct. For every v in F, H_v has no isolates and a W_v root of H_v-degree at least two; the empty selector is allowed.
claims.reason: The ordered first-mark partition and finite-graph deletion shadow prove each selected summand is nonpositive on the stated subclass. The vertex-cover identity records the low-cover shell regime but gives no bound on order-2k excesses. Trees with isolated marked roots or only degree-one marked roots retain boundary terms, and no selector-conditioned compensation across them has been proved.

limitations: No conclusion for eligible shell trees outside the stated per-selected-tag subclass; the explicit order-2k boundary excesses remain uncompensated.
No universal matching-resource inequality follows from the vertex-cover slack, and no counterexample to the complete selected sum is supplied.
The result uses exact combinatorial counting only; no computation, imported theorem, or formal verification was performed.
